headline: BOFA DROPS 2026 HAMMER: THREE RATE HIKES LOCKED IN — SILVER ALREADY PRICED IN THE SEPTEMBER BLOW
snippet: Bank of America published its most aggressive 2026 rate forecast on record — three 25-basis-point hikes in September, October, and December that would lift fed funds to 4.25–4.50% — and GoldSilver.com argues silver's 52% collapse from January's $121 peak has already priced in the September move, while today's May PCE print is the pivot test: a soft reading below 3.4% reopens gold's path to $4,300 and reverses the dollar surge; a hot print above 3.6% validates all three hikes. The Silver Institute's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit and China's structural solar-driven demand are unchanged — the question is whether the rate channel or the supply-demand channel controls the second half.

headline: BOFA EQUITY SCREEN FINDS GOLD MINERS PRICING IN $3,354 AU — 19% BELOW SPOT, CHEAPEST RELATIVE TO GOLD IN 3 YEARS
snippet: Bank of America's price-to-NAV screen across the full gold mining universe following the June 24 breach of $4,000 found that companies are on average implying a gold price of $3,354/oz — a 19% discount to spot at publication — meaning gold equities have underperformed even the metal in this correction and sit at their widest miner-to-metal valuation gap in roughly three years. BofA recommends the selloff as an entry opportunity, citing persistent US budget deficits and de-dollarisation trends as structural supports that no rate-hike cycle erases, and notes that the same institutional liquidation that created the discount mechanically reverses when rate expectations stabilise.

headline: WHY GOLD FALLS WHEN INFLATION RISES — EURONEWS UNPACKS THE HEDGE MYTH RETAIL INVESTORS STILL BELIEVE
snippet: Euronews published June 24 an explainer for investors confused by gold's 26% collapse from January highs despite inflation running above 3.7%: gold is not a short-term inflation hedge, it is a real interest rate hedge — when the Fed responds to inflation with rate hikes, rising real rates increase the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset, driving the institutional liquidation currently overwhelming physical demand. The recovery catalyst is not falling inflation but falling real rates, which won't arrive until the Fed pauses or markets stop pricing in additional hikes.

headline: GDX STOCHASTICS BOTTOMING — KITCO ANALYST: NEXT ENTRY IN MINERS LOOKS BETTER THAN BUYING GOLD ITSELF
snippet: A June 23 Kitco opinion argues that the coming bottom in gold mining stocks will represent a higher-quality entry than gold or silver directly: GDX's stochastics oscillator is approaching the oversold extreme that has historically preceded the largest multi-week recoveries in the gold equity complex, and producer operational leverage means a $500 gold recovery from the current floor would amplify into 30–50% gains for well-capitalised mid-tiers. The author recommends dollar-cost averaging into sustained weakness below the $3,900 gold zone rather than a single-point entry given the uncertainty around the exact seasonal trough.

headline: ORANO CANADA BACKS SKYHARBOUR 3,500m SUMMER URANIUM DRILL IN ATHABASCA BASIN — AGGT SURVEY LEADS
snippet: Orano Canada (operator, 79.2%) and Skyharbour Resources (TSXV: SYH, 20.8%) announced June 23 a comprehensive summer 2026 program at the 49,635-hectare Preston Lake Uranium Project in Saskatchewan's southwestern Athabasca Basin: a helicopter-borne Airborne Gravity Gradiometry survey covering the FSAN and Canoe Lake priority corridor — the two highest-priority targets from 2025's drilling — followed by a diamond drill campaign of up to 3,500 metres. Orano Canada's role as majority operator and funder adds institutional credibility at a time when U₃O₈ spot holds near $85/lb and the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust has accumulated more than 5 million pounds year-to-date.

headline: FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL CRACKS 71.9% Ni VIA ONSHORE MAX — AWARUITE DEPOSIT BYPASSES TRADITIONAL SMELTER CHAIN (TSXV:FAN)
source_name: GlobeNewswire / First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt (TSXV: FAN)
snippet: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) unveiled June 24 at the Fastmarkets Lithium Supply & Battery Raw Materials Conference in Las Vegas results from its proprietary ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) dry magnetic process, which upgraded RPM Zone rock samples from its Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project in Newfoundland to an average 67.4% nickel — peak 71.9% Ni, 1.76% Co — without conventional smelting, potentially allowing the company to sell a direct battery-grade alloy feed that bypasses Indonesian and Chinese refining infrastructure. At 71.9% nickel the concentrate approaches battery precursor purity thresholds, representing a meaningful processing milestone ahead of FAN's ongoing resource definition drilling in a market where Western battery supply chain independence is a strategic imperative.

headline: NOVAGOLD Q2: DONLIN GOLD BFS ON TRACK — $370M CASH, ONE ALASKA COURT RULING FROM A COMPLETE PERMIT STACK
snippet: NOVAGOLD (TSX/NYSE: NG) reported June 24 that all BFS engineering workstreams at the 39-million-ounce Donlin Gold project in Alaska — led by Fluor Corporation — advanced as planned through Q2 2026, with the comprehensive feasibility study on schedule for 2027 delivery, and cash resources of $370.2 million as of May 31 sufficient to complete the BFS without additional financing. The sole remaining challenge to Donlin's full permit stack — oral arguments in the Alaska Supreme Court regarding the Clean Water Act Section 401 certification — were heard in June and a ruling is now pending, meaning a favourable decision would leave the largest undeveloped gold project in North America with a legally complete permit package ahead of the 2027 construction decision.

headline: TERBIUM SURGES 22.8% IN JUNE TO $970/KG AS CHINA'S RARE EARTH PRICE INDEX HITS 261.9 — EXPORT CONTROLS BITE
snippet: China's rare earth markets extended their 2026 recovery through June with heavy rare earths leading: terbium surged 22.8% to $969.69/kg — nearly matching April's $970.18/kg peak — while the China Rare Earth Price Index reached 261.9 on June 23, driven by persistent MOFCOM export licence tightening across the sector. The +22.8% terbium move versus dysprosium's -5.5% softening illustrates a key structural point: terbium's 300–400 tonne annual global production volume makes it uniquely sensitive to any restriction in Chinese licence approvals, while dysprosium's 2,000+ tonne supply pool absorbs the same friction with far less price impact — a distinction that matters for investors evaluating which heavy rare earth plays carry the most operating leverage.

headline: GOLDSEEK: STOCHASTICS, CYCLES AND FUNDAMENTALS CONVERGE — "THE CYCLICAL LOW IS HERE" FOR GOLD AND GDX
snippet: A GoldSeek technical and cyclical analysis argues that three independent signals simultaneously converge on the current gold price zone as a cyclical low: GDX's stochastics oscillator is at the oversold level that preceded the three largest sustained gold stock rallies of this bull market; the 34-day price cycle is due to trough imminently; and the fundamental backdrop — central bank tonnage above 1,000 tonnes annually, ETF flows snapping their four-week outflow streak, and 13 of 14 major bank year-end targets above $4,800 — is the most structurally supportive at any correction low since the bull began. The author recommends nibblers enter now and more aggressive investors consider heavier positioning, noting that June seasonal weakness typically extends into early July but the risk-reward at $4,000 gold is the best since November 2025.

headline: GRASBERG MUDSLIDE, KAMOA ACID SHORTAGE, CHILE DOWN 9% — THREE SUPPLY SHOCKS BUILDING TOWARD 600,000-TONNE COPPER DEFICIT
snippet: Three concurrent mine supply shocks are converging on what Morgan Stanley forecasts as a 600,000-tonne refined copper deficit in 2026 — the largest in more than two decades: a fatal mudslide has curtailed Grasberg Block Cave output in Indonesia (representing ~70% of that mine's capacity), Kamoa-Kakula in the DRC is being production-limited by sulfuric acid shortages, and Chile's copper output fell 9.04% year-on-year in March to 434,314 tonnes. Combined with the June 30 Section 232 tariff decision — under which Goldman Sachs assigns high probability to a 25% refined copper import duty — the structural case for North American copper explorers with near-term development potential has rarely been more compelling.
